title: Frequency Tables, Dot Plots, Pictographs and Bar Graphs
seo_title: Grade 3 Data Worksheets: Frequency Tables, Dot Plots and Bar Graphs (TEKS 3.8A, 3.8B)
standard_text: 3.8A summarize a data set with multiple categories using a frequency table, dot plot, pictograph, or bar graph with scaled intervals; 3.8B solve one- and two-step problems using categorical data represented with a frequency table, dot plot, pictograph, or bar graph with scaled intervals
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 data worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.8A and 3.8B: tally marks and frequency tables, pictographs with a key, scaled bar graphs, dot plots and one- and two-step problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Read the key or the scale before you count.
key_sub: A picture or a grid space can stand for more than 1. Add or subtract the numbers you read to solve problems.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A frequency table lists each category and how many (often with tally marks).
  • A pictograph uses a key: if each picture is 2 students, 4 pictures mean 8 students.
  • A bar graph with scaled intervals counts by 2s, 5s or 10s. A bar between two lines is halfway between their numbers.
  • A dot plot shows one dot for each answer above its category.
  • To solve problems, read each number you need, then add or subtract. Some questions take two steps.

Examples

Example

A pictograph key says each star is 5 books. Maya's row has 3 stars. How many books?

3 stars × 5 books

Answer: 15 books

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting pictures without using the keyMultiply the number of pictures by the key.
Reading a bar between lines as the next lineHalfway between 10 and 20 on a scale of 10 is 15.
Stopping after one stepCheck what the question asks: in all, how many more, or how many fewer?

faq.a: Summarize a data set with several categories using a frequency table, dot plot, pictograph or bar graph with scaled intervals.
Solve one- and two-step problems using categorical data shown in a frequency table, dot plot, pictograph or bar graph with scaled intervals.
The amount between grid lines on a bar graph, such as 2, 5 or 10. It lets a graph show big numbers in a small space.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pictograph and a dot plot?
faq.a: A pictograph uses pictures and a key, so one picture can stand for more than 1. A dot plot uses one dot for each piece of data.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 1 group of 5 and 3 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 2 groups of 5 and 3 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 3 groups of 5 and 4 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 4 = 19.

items.q: What number do these tally marks show?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. Count the groups in 5s, then count on the single marks: 4 groups of 5 and 2 more: 4 × 5 = 20, and 20 + 2 = 22.
16 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 1, so look for 3 groups of 5 and 1 single mark. That is C. A shows 21 (one group of 5 too many); B shows 15 (one single mark is missing); D shows 17 (one single mark too many).

items.q: What number should go in the Frequency column for Skating?
items.e: The frequency is the number the tally marks show. Skating has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: Which sport got the most votes?
items.e: Skating has 14 votes (2 groups of 5 and 4 more). That is more than Sledding (11) and Volleyball (9).

items.q: How many more students chose sledding than snowboarding?
items.e: Sledding 11, snowboarding 4. How many more means find the difference: 11 − 4 = 7.

items.q: How many students voted altogether? (Each student voted once.)
items.e: Find the Skating frequency first: 14. Then add all the rows: 9 + 14 + 6 + 11 + 4 = 44.

items.q: How many families have 4 people?
items.e: Find the row for 4 people. The frequency is 10 (2 groups of 5). The 4 is the number of people, not the number of families.

items.q: What is the most common family size?
items.e: The biggest frequency is 10, in the row for 4 people. So 4 people is the most common family size. 10 is how many families, not how many people.

items.q: How many families are in the survey?
items.e: Add the frequencies: 3 + 8 + 10 + 5 + 2 = 28 families. (20 is 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6, the family sizes.)

items.q: How many families have more than 4 people?
items.e: More than 4 means 5 or 6 people: 5 + 2 = 7 families. Do not include the families with exactly 4 people. (17 adds the 4-people row too.)

items.q: How many more chickadees than cardinals were seen?
items.e: Chickadee 12, cardinal 8. How many more means subtract: 12 − 8 = 4.

items.q: Which bird was seen half as many times as the chickadee?
items.e: The chickadee was seen 12 times. Half of 12 is 6. The blue jay has a frequency of 6.

items.q: Owen sees 4 more sparrows. What is the new frequency for Sparrow?
items.e: The sparrow frequency was 15. 4 more means add: 15 + 4 = 19.

items.q: Which survey question has answers that are numbers?
c: How many pets do you have?
What is your favorite winter sport?
How do you get to school?
items.e: “How many pets do you have?” has number answers, such as 0, 1, 2 or 3 (quantitative data). The other questions have answers that are words, such as red, bus or volleyball (qualitative data).

items.q: Which survey question has answers that are words, not numbers?
c: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
How many books did you read this week?
How many people are in your family?
items.e: Favorite fruit gives answers like apple or banana. These are words (qualitative data). The other questions ask “how many”, so the answers are numbers.

items.q: Noah makes a tally of the wild geese that fly over the schoolyard. He draws 4 groups of five and 3 single marks. How many geese has he counted?
items.e: Each group of five shows 5: 5, 10, 15, 20. Then 3 more: 21, 22, 23. So 23 geese. (Counting each group as 4 gives 19.)

items.q: Sofia counted 17 votes for snowboarding. How should she draw the tally?
items.e: 17 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 2. Draw 3 groups of five (four lines and one across) and 2 single marks. Never leave 5 or more single marks: make another group of five.

items.q: How many cups of lemonade were sold on Tuesday?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 cups. The Tue row has 1 circle and half a circle: 1 × 2 = 2, and half of 2 is 1, so 2 + 1 = 3 cups.
Each star stands for 5 cans. The Room 2 row has 7 stars: 7 × 5 = 35 cans.

items.q: How many vanilla cones were sold?
items.e: Each square stands for 10 cones. The Vanilla row has 4 squares and half a square: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 cones.

items.q: How many students have a fish?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 students. The Fish row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 students.
Each star stands for 10 stickers. The Ruby row has 6 stars and half a star: 6 × 10 = 60, and half of 10 is 5, so 60 + 5 = 65 stickers.

items.q: How many shells did Sam find?
items.e: Each square stands for 5 shells. The Sam row has 4 squares: 4 × 5 = 20 shells.

items.q: How many days were rainy?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 days. The Rainy row has 5 circles and half a circle: 5 × 2 = 10, and half of 2 is 1, so 10 + 1 = 11 days.
Each star stands for 10 students. The Pizza row has 6 stars: 6 × 10 = 60 students.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each square stands for 5 votes. The Apple row has 2 squares: 2 × 5 = 10 votes.

items.q: How many votes did Winter get?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 votes. The Winter row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 votes.
Each star stands for 5 students. The Soccer row has 6 stars: 6 × 5 = 30 students.

items.q: How many students walk to school?
items.e: Each square stands for 10 students. The Walk row has 6 squares: 6 × 10 = 60 students.

items.q: How many robins were seen?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 birds. The Robin row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 2 = 4, and half of 2 is 1, so 4 + 1 = 5 birds.
Every star has the same value, so the row with the most stars wins. The Oak row has 7 stars: 7 × 5 = 35 trees.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest books?
items.e: Every square has the same value, so the row with the fewest squares wins. The Sports row has 2 squares: 2 × 10 = 20 books.

items.q: Which row shows the most books?
items.e: Every circle has the same value, so the row with the most circles wins. The Leo row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 books.
The key says one whole star = 2 points. Half a star is half of 2, which is 1 point.

items.q: In this graph, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 votes. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 votes.

items.q: Which row shows 30 students?
items.e: 30 students ÷ 5 = 6, so look for a row with 6 circles. The Car row has 6 circles: 6 × 5 = 30 students.
60 students ÷ 10 = 6, so look for a row with 6 stars. The Pasta row has 6 stars: 6 × 10 = 60 students.

items.q: How many books did Ben read?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Ben bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 books.

items.q: How many votes did Green get?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Green bar ends at the line for 5. So the answer is 5 votes.

items.q: How many students chose tacos?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Tacos bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. So the answer is 35 students.

items.q: How many stickers does Omar have?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Omar bar ends halfway between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. So the answer is 11 stickers.

items.q: How many points did the Hawks score?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Hawks bar ends at the line for 30. So the answer is 30 points.

items.q: How many finches were seen?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Finch bar ends at the line for 25. So the answer is 25 birds.

items.q: How many mint cones were sold?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Mint bar ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25. So the answer is 25 cones.

items.q: How many votes did Grape get?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Grape bar ends at the line for 14. So the answer is 14 votes.

items.q: How many students chose soccer?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Soccer bar ends at the line for 35. So the answer is 35 students.

items.q: How many cans did Room 1 collect?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Room 1 bar ends at the line for 20. So the answer is 20 cans.

items.q: How many days were cloudy?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Cloudy bar ends at the line for 4. So the answer is 4 days.

items.q: How many shells did Owen find?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Owen bar ends at the line for 30. So the answer is 30 shells.

items.q: How many Space books were checked out?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Space bar ends halfway between 50 and 60, so it shows 55. So the answer is 55 books.

items.q: How many students have a cat?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Cat bar ends at the line for 10. So the answer is 10 students.

items.q: How many students ride the bus to school?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Bus bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. So the answer is 35 students.

items.q: Which bar shows 25 trees?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. Find 25 on the scale. The Oak bar ends at the line for 25.

items.q: Which bar shows 14 cups?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. Find 14 on the scale. The Thu bar ends at the line for 14.

items.q: Which bar shows 25 votes?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. Find 25 on the scale. The Spring bar ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25.

items.q: Which bar shows the most students?
items.e: The Walk bar is the tallest one. The Walk bar ends at the line for 30. It shows 30 students.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest students?
items.e: The Baseball bar is the shortest one. The Baseball bar ends at the line for 2. It shows 2 students.

items.q: Each dot is 1 student. How many students chose Bird?
items.e: Count the dots above Bird: 5.

items.q: How many students are shown in the dot plot in all?
items.e: Add the dots in every column: 8 + 6 + 5 = 19.

items.q: Which choice has the most dots?
items.e: The Fish column of dots is tallest: Fish (9).

items.q: Which choice has the fewest dots?
items.e: The Rainy column of dots is shortest: Rainy (1).

items.q: Each dot is 1 student. How many students chose Football?
items.e: Count the dots above Football: 2.

items.q: Which choice has the fewest dots?
items.e: The Rainy column of dots is shortest: Rainy (2).

items.q: Which choice has the fewest dots?
items.e: The Mockingbird column of dots is shortest: Mockingbird (1).

items.q: Each dot is 1 student. How many students chose Longhorn?
items.e: Count the dots above Longhorn: 8.

How many students are shown in the dot plot in all?
items.e: Add the dots in every column: 1 + 8 + 2 = 11.

items.q: Which choice has the most dots?
items.e: The Cloudy column of dots is tallest: Cloudy (9).

items.q: Which choice has the most dots?
items.e: The Armadillo column of dots is tallest: Armadillo (4).

items.q: Which choice has the fewest dots?
items.e: The Baseball column of dots is shortest: Baseball (4).

items.q: Each dot is 1 student. How many students chose Cloudy?
items.e: Count the dots above Cloudy: 6.

items.q: How many students are shown in the dot plot in all?
items.e: Add the dots in every column: 1 + 9 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Each dot is 1 student. How many students chose Walk?
items.e: Count the dots above Walk: 6.

items.q: Which choice has the fewest dots?
items.e: The Walk column of dots is shortest: Walk (2).

Each dot is 1 student. How many students chose Car?
items.e: Count the dots above Car: 2.

items.q: How many students are shown in the dot plot in all?
items.e: Add the dots in every column: 3 + 2 + 7 + 8 = 20.

items.q: How many more cups were sold on Friday than on Tuesday?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Fri bar ends at the line for 12. The Tue bar ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it shows 7. 12 − 7 = 5, so the answer is 5 more cups.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Spring get than Fall?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Fall bar ends at the line for 20. The Spring bar ends at the line for 5. 20 − 5 = 15, so the answer is 15 fewer votes.

items.q: How many more Animals books than Space books were checked out?
items.e: The Animals row has 7 squares: 7 × 10 = 70 books. The Space row has 2 squares: 2 × 10 = 20 books. 70 − 20 = 50, so the answer is 50 more books.

items.q: How many fewer books did Noah read than Ava?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Ava bar ends at the line for 12. The Noah bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. 12 − 3 = 9, so the answer is 9 fewer books.

items.q: How many more cans did Room 4 collect than Room 2?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Room 4 bar ends at the line for 30. The Room 2 bar ends at the line for 20. 30 − 20 = 10, so the answer is 10 more cans.

items.q: How many fewer points did the Lions score than the Hawks?
items.e: The Hawks row has 7 squares: 7 × 10 = 70 points. The Lions row has 4 squares: 4 × 10 = 40 points. 70 − 40 = 30, so the answer is 30 fewer points.

items.q: How many more votes did Yellow get than Green?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Yellow bar ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. The Green bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. 65 − 35 = 30, so the answer is 30 more votes.

items.q: How many fewer students have a fish than a hamster?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Hamster bar ends at the line for 14. The Fish bar ends at the line for 2. 14 − 2 = 12, so the answer is 12 fewer students.

items.q: How many more shells did Sam find than Nora?
items.e: The Sam row has 6 squares: 6 × 5 = 30 shells. The Nora row has 2 squares: 2 × 5 = 10 shells. 30 − 10 = 20, so the answer is 20 more shells.

items.q: How many fewer maple trees than oak trees are in the park?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Oak bar ends halfway between 50 and 60, so it shows 55. The Maple bar ends at the line for 50. 55 − 50 = 5, so the answer is 5 fewer trees.

items.q: How many votes were there in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Purple 11, Red 6, Blue 8, Yellow 12. Step 2: add them: 11 + 6 + 8 + 12 = 37 votes.

items.q: How many trees are in the park in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Maple 25, Oak 30, Pine 5, Birch 15. Step 2: add them: 25 + 30 + 5 + 15 = 75 trees.

items.q: How many books were checked out in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Space 70, Sports 45, Mystery 50, Animals 65. Step 2: add them: 70 + 45 + 50 + 65 = 230 books.

items.q: How many votes were there in all?
items.e: Step 1: read every bar: Pear 20, Banana 25, Orange 35, Grape 5. Step 2: add them: 20 + 25 + 35 + 5 = 85 votes.

items.q: How many more cups do the Mon and Thu bars show together than the Wed bar?
items.e: Step 1: Mon + Thu = 50 + 20 = 70. Step 2: compare with Wed (60): 70 − 60 = 10, so 10 more cups.

items.q: How many more days do the Rainy and Windy bars show together than the Sunny bar?
items.e: Step 1: Rainy + Windy = 10 + 6 = 16. Step 2: compare with Sunny (12): 16 − 12 = 4, so 4 more days.

items.q: How many more stickers do the Kai and Grace bars show together than the Lily bar?
items.e: Step 1: Kai + Grace = 15 + 25 = 40. Step 2: compare with Lily (35): 40 − 35 = 5, so 5 more stickers.

items.q: How many more students do the Bike and Bus bars show together than the Walk bar?
items.e: Step 1: Bike + Bus = 60 + 20 = 80. Step 2: compare with Walk (70): 80 − 70 = 10, so 10 more students.

items.q: How many votes were not for Spring?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 5 + 35 + 10 + 20 = 70. Step 2: take away Spring (5): 70 − 5 = 65 votes. Or add the other three bars: 35 + 10 + 20 = 65.

items.q: How many students did not choose swimming?
items.e: Step 1: add all the bars: 70 + 30 + 20 + 10 = 130. Step 2: take away Swimming (10): 130 − 10 = 120 students. Or add the other three bars: 70 + 30 + 20 = 120.
